spec.description: CWN Network Operations — abstracted AP telemetry. v12 brings AP2 (192.168.1.101, mesh-connected over 802.11s on phy1-mesh0) fully online: 'Node status', 'AP Resource Health', and the station health table are now genuinely parametrized by $ap (job="openwrt-$ap-node"/"openwrt-$ap-wifi"), which the v10/v11 description had already announced but the dashboard did not yet implement. Two fixed 'AP1/AP2 status' panels are added alongside the $ap-driven ones so node availability is visible without using the dropdown. New 'Mesh Backhaul' row exposes SNR, signal, and packet-loss on the AP1↔AP2 802.11s link (phy1-mesh0), reported from AP1's side as the canonical, non-duplicated view of the (symmetric) link. v12.1 patch: added job="openwrt-ap1-qdisc" filter to the Network Health Check WiFi-side term and job="openwrt-ap1-mesh-qdisc" filter to the new Mesh Backhaul packet-loss panel, closing a label-collision gap that would have silently summed AP1 and AP2s qdisc series together once AP2s own qdisc exporter went live. v12.1: connected-clients count now sums AP1+AP2 (was AP1-only); added per-node 'Issues — AP1'/'Issues — AP2' triage panels to Operator Actions Needed, counting CPU, memory, link-flap, and qdisc-loss threshold breaches per node. v12.2: 'Issues — AP1'/'Issues — AP2' replaced with a single 'Network Issue Summary' panel switching between three message states via a 25-way composite value mapping. Mesh SNR and Mesh RSSI panels now show a Weak/Fair/Good-style verdict with plain-language narration instead of the raw dB/dBm number, matching the rest of the dashboard's house style (Signal quality, Link stability, etc). v12.3: the four continuous/gradual-fault indicators (QoE RTT, WiFi Channel Saturation, Gateway Bandwidth Saturation, and Signal Quality) now show a sparkline trend alongside their value and colour, so degradation is visible as it develops rather than only once a threshold is crossed — directly targeting the H4 mechanism (gradual faults benefit more from visual prioritisation than discrete ones). QoE RTT and WiFi Channel Saturation were converted from a discretized 0/1/2 verdict to the raw metric with equivalent range-based text mappings, so the same plain-language narration is preserved. Signal Quality (panel-7) has also been RESTORED — it was absent from v12.2 entirely, leaving the 'Wireless signal degradation' task with no panel. v12.3.1 patch: fixed non-exhaustive range mappings on panel-16 and panel-307 that could fall back to displaying a raw unmapped number (observed: a 100,200ms RTT reading fell just outside the old 200-100000ms 'red' band). Panel-307's mapping now also explicitly handles the -1 sentinel link_util.sh writes when no survey data is available, instead of silently showing '-1%'. Restored original legend names (Internet Speed, WiFi Airtime) lost in v12.3. v12.3.2 patch: the v12.3.1 range mappings were structurally invalid — Grafana's RangeMap schema allows exactly one {from,to,result} range per mapping object, not several nested under one object the way value-type mappings work. Rebuilt as a flat list of single-range mapping objects (one per band) on panel-16, panel-307, and panel-7, which is why thresholds (colour) were rendering correctly while the mapped narrative text was silently falling back to the raw number even for in-range values. v12.3.3: fixed the Gateway Bandwidth Saturation stacking bug (reduceOptions.values was true, harmless under the old instant query, but rendered every timestamp as a separate row once converted to a range query for the sparkline). Added AP Resource Health (CPU & Memory) to the continuous-fault sparkline treatment — it was missing from the original categorisation. v12.3.4: Mesh link SNR and Mesh link signal (RSSI) panels now carry the same raw-value-plus-sparkline-plus-range-mapping treatment as the client-facing continuous indicators, rather than the earlier PromQL-discretised verdict pattern. Mesh link packet loss (panel-512) has not yet been converted; flagged for a follow-up pass for consistency. All three mesh backhaul panels (clarity/SNR, strength/RSSI, reliability/packet loss) now carry the same raw-value-plus-sparkline-plus-range-mapping treatment and plain-language labelling as the client-facing continuous indicators. v13: redesigned at-a-glance layout. New Network Health % composite gauge (equal-weighted average of 8 normalised sub-scores; documented as a placeholder for future operator-criticality weighting). New fixed, simultaneously-visible AP1 and AP2 rows, each grouping CPU, Memory, Packet Loss, and Signal Quality for that specific node regardless of the $ap dropdown -- Signal Quality substituted for the originally-sketched 'Latency' cell, since latency has no genuine per-AP measurement in this architecture (only a single shared gateway-wide QoE probe), and no metric was fabricated to fill that slot. Network-wide metrics (QoE latency, DNS health, bandwidth) given their own row. The $ap-templated deep-dive section and all detailed rows (mesh backhaul, traffic, link stability, packet loss/DHCP) from v12.3.5 are preserved below, unchanged, for drill-down.

spec.title: Station health table — $ap (phy0-ap0)
spec.description: Per-station WiFi health table for the node selected in the AP Node dropdown above. v12.3.4 fix: added device="phy0-ap0" filter to every station-level query, which was previously missing entirely. Without it, the table silently included stations from every radio on the selected node, including the 802.11s mesh peer on phy1-mesh0, mislabeled alongside genuine phy0-ap0 clients despite the panel title already stating phy0-ap0 only.

spec.title: Top Applications by Data Volume (24 hrs)
spec.description: Top applications by data volume, addressing the survey finding that 3/3 operators want per-application data usage visibility, and reflecting the heavy-hitter traffic concentration observed in the CN measurement study (up to 86.8% of volume from 4 applications).

spec.title: Total Data Consumption (24hrs)
spec.description: Total data consumption (network accounting) alongside how it compares to your expected daily baseline ($avg_daily_consumption_gb, editable dashboard variable). Percentage verdict: green <50%, orange 50-75%, red >=75% of that baseline.

spec.title: Gateway Bandwidth Saturation (Upload / Download)
spec.description: Internet uplink (WAN) saturation, shown separately for upload and download since this backhaul is asymmetric ($wan_capacity_mbps_up / $wan_capacity_mbps_down, editable dashboard variables). A single combined figure would misrepresent whichever direction has the smaller capacity. Detects the shared, network-wide bottleneck operators specifically flagged in the survey ('no way to know if network has reached capacity') — distinct from radio congestion. High usage here with a clear WiFi Channel verdict points to too many concurrent heavy users or heavy-hitter apps (cf. traffic structure findings) saturating the actual Internet connection, not the local radio. v12.3: sparkline trend added; thresholds and value were already raw. v12.3.3 fix: reduceOptions.values was true (harmless under the old instant query, since only one sample existed). Once switched to a range query for the sparkline, this rendered every sample in the time window as a stacked row instead of one reduced value. Set to false.

spec.title: AP Resource Health — CPU & Memory ($ap)
spec.description: AP router CPU and memory, each against its own literature-grounded threshold. CPU: 70%/90% (Harchol-Balter; PASTRAMI 2024; Agarwal et al.) -- sustained high CPU on a single-core MIPS AP indicates overload. Memory: 80%/90%, following the Nagios check_mem convention (warning below 20% free, critical below 10% free). v12.3.3: added to the continuous-fault sparkline treatment — device resource exhaustion (CPU/memory climbing toward saturation) is a gradual signal, the same category as QoE RTT, WiFi Channel Saturation, Bandwidth Saturation, and Signal Quality, and had been omitted from the original H4 continuous/discrete categorisation.

spec.title: Connection Speed (QoE)
spec.description: QoE verdict driven by P90 (tail) latency rather than average RTT, per the CN measurement study finding that tail-latency variability drives user-perceived performance more than mean delay. Thresholds are informed by the baseline-vs-effective RTT divergence observed in the Malawi and South Africa CN traces (indicative — tune per deployment). v12.3: now displays raw P90 RTT (ms) with a sparkline trend, instead of the discretized 0/1/2 verdict, so gradual degradation is visible before it crosses a threshold.

result.text: Elevated — some users may notice delays
Degraded — connection is slow, check for heavy use or contact your provider

spec.title: Name Resolution (DNS Health)
spec.description: DNS health verdict from the ratio of failed responses (NXDOMAIN/NOTIMP) to total queries. Grounded in the CN measurement study's finding that DNS failures are heavily concentrated among a small number of destinations — a rising failure ratio points to resolver misconfiguration, upstream reliability issues, or possible DGA/malicious traffic.

spec.title: Packet Loss
spec.description: Packet loss ratio measured on active QoE probes (iperf/ping-derived) between the gateway and Internet. Elevated loss degrades real-time applications (VoIP, video calls) disproportionately, per operator-reported frustration with 'packet loss' as a regular issue.

spec.title: Jitter
spec.description: Inter-packet delay variation on active QoE probes. High jitter degrades VoIP/video call quality even when average latency and loss remain acceptable.

spec.title: DHCP Pool Available
spec.description: Share of the DHCP address pool still available for new clients, from the DHCP lease exporter. Low availability means new devices cannot obtain an IP address — the DHCP allocation failure condition named directly by the Colnodo operator.

spec.title: DHCP Health
spec.description: DHCP health verdict from remaining pool capacity. A pool nearing exhaustion means the next client to associate will fail to obtain an address — expand the pool or investigate stale leases before this reaches zero.

0.text: Pool exhausted — clients failing to obtain IP, expand pool

spec.title: Link flaps (15m)-($ap)
spec.description: AP interface link flap events in the last hour. 0 = stable.

spec.title: WiFi Channel Saturation
spec.description: Radio medium (airtime) saturation, from channel-busy-time ratio via 'iw survey dump' on the AP itself. Detects contention/interference/retransmission load independent of backhaul usage — e.g. many weak-signal clients can saturate airtime even when the Internet uplink is nearly idle. High airtime use with low Gateway Bandwidth usage points to channel congestion, not an Internet-capacity problem — consider changing channel, reducing channel width, or adding an AP. v12.3: now displays raw channel utilization (%) with a sparkline trend instead of the discretized 0/1/2 verdict.

result.text: No data — survey unavailable, check exporter

spec.title: Acess Point 1 status
spec.description: Fixed reachability check for ap1, shown independently of the AP Node dropdown so both nodes' availability is visible at a glance without switching.

spec.title: Access Point 2 status
spec.description: Fixed reachability check for ap2, shown independently of the AP Node dropdown so both nodes' availability is visible at a glance without switching.

spec.title: Mesh link clarity (AP1 ↔ AP2) — SNR
spec.description: Verdict derived from raw mesh SNR on phy1-mesh0 (AP1's side, canonical). 0-12.4dB=Weak, 12.5-24.9dB=Fair, >=25dB=Good. v12.3.4 fix: converted from a PromQL-discretised 0/1/2 verdict to the raw SNR value with a sparkline trend and exhaustive range-based text mapping, matching the treatment already applied to client-facing continuous indicators. Was previously excluded from trend treatment on scope grounds (not among the ten Phase Three indicators), not because it is not a genuinely continuous metric. Panel title and inline label renamed to plain-language wording, matching the precedent set by the QoE panel (P90 RTT -> Internet Speed) in v12.3.1; the technical acronym is retained parenthetically in the title for engineers/examiners without being the primary label an operator reads.

result.text: Fair — monitor, may need attention soon

spec.title: Mesh link strength (AP1 ↔ AP2) — RSSI
spec.description: Verdict derived from raw mesh RSSI on phy1-mesh0 (AP1's side, canonical). <=-90dBm=Weak, -89 to -71dBm=Moderate, >=-70dBm=Strong. v12.3.4 fix: converted from a PromQL-discretised 0/1/2 verdict to the raw RSSI value with a sparkline trend and exhaustive range-based text mapping, for the same reason as panel-510. Panel title and inline label renamed to plain-language wording, matching the precedent set by the QoE panel (P90 RTT -> Internet Speed) in v12.3.1; the technical acronym is retained parenthetically in the title for engineers/examiners without being the primary label an operator reads.

result.text: Moderate — usable, keep an eye on it

spec.title: Mesh link reliability (AP1 ↔ AP2) — Packet Loss
spec.description: Drop-to-attempted-packet ratio on the mesh backhaul interface phy1-mesh0, using the same qdisc-based formula as the existing Network Health Check's Wi-Fi-side term, retargeted from phy0-ap0 to phy1-mesh0. If AP2 loses backhaul, clients still associated to AP2 lose Internet access even though AP2 itself may still show 'Online.' [v12.1: now reads from the dedicated wifi_qdisc_health_mesh.sh / job="openwrt-ap1-mesh-qdisc" scrape target, not the AP-facing qdisc job.] v12.3.4 fix: brought in line with panel-510/panel-511 -- added a sparkline trend (graphMode area, range query), exhaustive range-based narrative mapping reusing the same 2.5%/5% packet-loss thresholds already established for the client-facing Connection Reliability panel, and a plain-language title/label, closing the asymmetry left when SNR and RSSI were fixed first.

result.text: Degraded — some packets being dropped, monitor
Unreliable — mesh link dropping significant traffic

spec.description: Fixed to AP1 regardless of the \$ap dropdown, so both AP rows are visible at once. Same 70/90 thresholds and formula as the \$ap-templated deep-dive panel.

spec.title: Memory (ap1)
spec.description: Fixed to AP1. Same 70/90 thresholds and formula as the \$ap-templated deep-dive panel.

spec.title: Packet loss (ap1)
spec.description: Fixed to AP1's client-facing radio (phy0-ap0), using the same qdisc-based accounting and 2.5%/5% thresholds already established for the mesh reliability panel, reused here for the client side.

spec.title: CPU (ap2)
spec.description: Fixed to AP2 regardless of the \$ap dropdown, so both AP rows are visible at once. Same 70/90 thresholds and formula as the \$ap-templated deep-dive panel.

spec.description: Fixed to AP2. Same 70/90 thresholds and formula as the \$ap-templated deep-dive panel.

spec.title: Packet loss (ap2)
spec.description: Fixed to AP2's client-facing radio (phy0-ap0), using the same qdisc-based accounting and 2.5%/5% thresholds already established for the mesh reliability panel, reused here for the client side.

spec.title: Network Health %
spec.description: Composite score averaging eight normalised sub-scores (CPU, memory, client packet loss, signal quality, wireless airtime -- each averaged across AP1 and AP2 -- plus gateway-wide QoE latency, DNS failure ratio, and bandwidth saturation), each mapped onto a 0-100 scale using the same green/orange/red thresholds already established for that metric elsewhere on this dashboard. Currently equal-weighted (1/8 each) as a documented default; the intended refinement is to replace these equal weights with the Phase Two Component B operator criticality ranking (Section on the Importance-Performance diagnostic), so the score reflects what operators actually said matters most, rather than an arbitrary equal split.

spec.name: wan_capacity_mbps_up
spec.label: WAN Upload Capacity (Mbps)
spec.description: Known Internet uplink capacity in Mbps (upload direction). Set to your actual backhaul plan speed. Split from download capacity because this backhaul is asymmetric.

spec.name: wan_capacity_mbps_down
spec.label: WAN Download Capacity (Mbps)
spec.description: Known Internet downlink capacity in Mbps (download direction). Set to your actual backhaul plan speed. Split from upload capacity because this backhaul is asymmetric.

spec.name: avg_daily_consumption_gb
spec.label: Avg Daily Data Consumption (GB)
spec.description: Expected average daily data consumption in GB. Used as the baseline the Data Consumption panel's percentage verdict is measured against (green <50%, orange 50-75%, red >=75%).

spec.name: ap
spec.label: AP Node
spec.description: AP node selector. 'Network at a Glance' (deep-dive panel), 'AP Resource Health', and the station health table now use $ap as of v12. The Mesh Backhaul row is intentionally NOT gated by $ap, since it shows one link between both nodes, not a per-node metric.
